events.title: Overwintering Fires Reignite in Fort Providence and Whatì, NWT
events.detail: Fires that had smouldered underground since 2025 evacuations reignited near Fort Providence and Whatì, Northwest Territories in late April — an early warning sign of the dry conditions that would drive the NWT to the highest hectares-burned total of any jurisdiction this season.

events.title: Dryden 11 Fire Shuts Highway 599, Ontario
events.detail: A 168-hectare wildfire (Dryden 11) ignited near Sandbar Lake Provincial Park in northwestern Ontario, prompting evacuations and the closure of Highway 599 — an early sign of the dry, high-danger conditions that would define the 2026 season.

events.title: First Firefighter Death of the Season — Moschelle Fire, Nova Scotia
events.detail: A 40-year-old firefighter died of a sudden medical emergency while battling the 1.19-hectare Moschelle Fire in Annapolis County, Nova Scotia — the season's first fatality, months before the peak of the crisis.

events.title: Lightning Sparks Four Fires in Wood Buffalo National Park, NWT
events.detail: A lightning storm ignited four wildfires inside Wood Buffalo National Park, Northwest Territories. The largest grew to roughly 35,288 hectares by May 29, an early signal of the extreme lightning-driven activity that would hit the NWT hardest of any jurisdiction this season.

events.title: Lobstick Fire Crosses North Saskatchewan River, Threatens Prince Albert Homes
events.detail: The Lobstick Fire near Prince Albert, Saskatchewan crossed the North Saskatchewan River and burned roughly 19,000 hectares, threatening homes and destroying an estimated $20–25 million in commercial timber.

events.title: Structural Fires Near Thunder Lake Provincial Park, Alberta
events.detail: Alberta Wildfire issued a fire advisory for the Fort McMurray Forest Area as structural fires south of Thunder Lake Provincial Park prompted an evacuation alert; 13 properties were impacted and six buildings destroyed.

events.title: Timmins 9 Fire Forces Mattagami First Nation Evacuation
events.detail: The Timmins 9 fire grew to approximately 3,300 hectares, forcing more than 160 residents of Mattagami First Nation to evacuate before the fire was contained on June 15 — one of the first First Nations evacuations of the season.

events.title: Kalamoir Park Fire Prompts West Kelowna Evacuation
events.detail: An 8-hectare human-caused fire in West Kelowna, BC's Kalamoir Park forced roughly 800 people from 357 properties to evacuate; the order was lifted within days as crews contained the blaze.

events.title: Aerial Firefighting Plane Crash Kills 3 Near Fort Simpson, NWT
events.detail: A Buffalo Airways Rockwell Aero Commander 690 crashed roughly 50 km from Fort Simpson, Northwest Territories while responding to a wildfire, killing the pilot and two firefighters — the deadliest single incident of the season.

events.title: Fort Simpson and Wrigley Ordered to Evacuate to Yellowknife
events.detail: An out-of-control fire roughly 7 km west of Fort Simpson Airport forced immediate evacuation of most of the community's 1,300 residents, along with 130 people from Wrigley. Most evacuees sheltered in Yellowknife.

events.title: Labrador Wildfires Trigger State of Emergency, Canada Day Cancelled
events.detail: Lightning-sparked fires including the Walsh River fire (472 ha) near Labrador City prompted evacuation orders for Walsh River, Tamarack Golf Course, Duley Lake and Throne Lake — about 120 residents evacuated within a 30 km radius. Canada Day celebrations were postponed in St. John's, Labrador City and Happy Valley-Goose Bay.

events.title: Walsh River Fire Downgraded, Labrador West Residents Return
events.detail: The Walsh River fire near Labrador City was downgraded to "held" status, allowing residents to return home after a roughly 10-day evacuation. Nova Scotia crews had arrived days earlier to reinforce Newfoundland and Labrador firefighters.

events.title: Thunder Bay 36 Fire Forms in Wabakimi Provincial Park
events.detail: Several smaller fires merged into what would become Thunder Bay 36 in the Wabakimi Provincial Park area of northwestern Ontario. Within weeks it grew into the largest wildfire ever recorded in Ontario.

events.title: Toronto Ranked Worst Air Quality of Any Major City in the World
events.detail: Wildfire smoke from over 180 active Ontario fires (136 in the northwest) turned Toronto's skies orange; IQAir ranked Toronto's air quality the worst of any major city in the world, ahead of Kinshasa and New Delhi. An orange weather alert was issued and Toronto General/Western hospitals logged 36 air-quality-related ER visits.

events.title: Namaygoosisagagun (Collins) First Nation Evacuates by Boat, Later Destroyed
events.detail: Residents of Namaygoosisagagun First Nation fled by boat as wildfire swept into the community; the settlement was later destroyed by the fire, becoming a flashpoint in criticism of the province's warning systems.

events.title: Milwaukee Records All-Time-High AQI of 644
events.detail: Canadian wildfire smoke pushed Milwaukee's Air Quality Index to 644 at roughly 12:30pm — more than double the city's previous record of 300, set in 1987, and far beyond the EPA's standard 0–500 scale.

events.title: 16+ US States Under Air Quality Alerts; Venues and Airports Disrupted
events.detail: AQI readings hit 1,135 in Saginaw, MI, 1,615 in Virginia, MN, 576 in Cleveland and 460 in Detroit. Cedar Point amusement park closed early, a Cleveland Guardians–Pittsburgh Pirates game was suspended, and a ground delay was later issued at Philadelphia International Airport. More than 120 million Americans lived under air quality alerts during the episode.

events.title: CN Rail Suspends Operations Near Armstrong, Ontario
events.detail: CN Rail suspended operations near Armstrong, Ontario as wildfires closed in on the community; evacuation orders were also issued for Armstrong, Lac La Croix, Lac des Mille Lacs and Gull Bay First Nations the same day.

events.title: Michigan Republican Delegation Presses Carney on Smoke Accountability
events.detail: Four members of Michigan's Republican congressional delegation sent a letter to Prime Minister Mark Carney demanding accountability for wildfire smoke crossing into the United States, opening a summer of cross-border political friction over the fires.

events.title: Canadian Armed Forces Airlift Eabametoong First Nation
events.detail: The CAF received a Request for Federal Assistance and deployed four CC-130J Hercules aircraft to evacuate Eabametoong First Nation (Fort Hope), flying out about 600 of the community's more than 1,600 residents as a wildfire advanced.

events.title: Trump Threatens Tariffs Over Canadian Wildfire Smoke
events.detail: Donald Trump posted on Truth Social threatening tariffs on Canada over wildfire smoke drifting into the US, saying Washington is "holding Canada responsible" for forest management and that smoke-related costs "must of necessity" be added to Canada's tariffs. Ontario Premier Doug Ford called the rhetoric "unacceptable."

events.title: Pikangikum First Nation: 2,000 Evacuated to Toronto Area
events.detail: About 2,000 residents of Pikangikum First Nation began relocating to Mississauga and Toronto as the Red Lake 62 fire, covering roughly 26,000 hectares, threatened the community.

events.title: First Nations Leaders Demand Inquiry, Call Response "Unacceptable"
events.detail: First Nations leaders from across northwestern Ontario held a joint news conference challenging Premier Doug Ford's account of the wildfire response, citing delayed warnings and coordination gaps, and demanding a public inquiry and removal of MNR leadership.

events.title: PM Carney Convenes Federal Incident Response Group
events.detail: Prime Minister Mark Carney convened the Incident Response Group to be briefed on wildfire activity burning in every province and territory, and reaffirmed federal support including CAF airlift capacity and CIFFC coordination.

events.title: NYC Air Quality Spikes, Then Flash Flooding Grounds Flights
events.detail: New York City's air quality index reached 173 before overnight rain cleared the smoke — but the same storm system caused flash flooding, hundreds of flight delays and a ground stop at Newark Liberty International Airport.

events.title: DBRS Morningstar: Wildfires Not Yet Threatening Insurer Balance Sheets
events.detail: Rating agency Morningstar DBRS assessed that despite the scale of the 2026 season, wildfire losses were not severely eroding Canadian insurers' balance sheets — though the report flagged compounding pressure from tariffs and adjuster shortages on claims processing.

events.title: US Senate Rejects Trump's Demand for Canadian Wildfire Damages
events.detail: Republican and Democratic senators rejected President Trump's demand that Canada pay damages over wildfire smoke, with scientists testifying the extreme season is attributable to climate change rather than Canadian forest-management failures. Sen. Bernie Moreno's sanctions bill did not advance.

events.title: Thunder Bay 36 Confirmed Largest Wildfire in Ontario History
events.detail: Thunder Bay 36 grew to nearly 320,000 hectares, confirmed as the largest wildfire ever recorded in Ontario — surpassing all prior benchmarks by a wide margin as it continued to burn out of control.

events.title: Pear Lake Fire Destroys Structures Near Clinton, BC
events.detail: The Pear Lake Fire destroyed structures across roughly 120 properties near Clinton, BC, with the Okanagan Indian Band reporting close to 200 homes lost in the nearby Vernon area — one of the season's costliest structure-loss events in the Okanagan.

events.title: Over 5,000 Evacuated on West Side of Okanagan Lake
events.detail: More than 5,000 people were evacuated from the west side of Okanagan Lake, BC, as fires spread through the region; widespread power outages affected thousands of additional residents.

events.title: Bald Range Fire Erupts Near Summerland, BC — "Like a Bomb Going Off"
events.detail: The Bald Range fire ignited around 5:30pm and grew from 50 to 95 km² within 24 hours, with flames reaching over 61 metres and generating pyrocumulus clouds with self-sustaining fire lightning. Premier David Eby relayed the fire commander's description: "like a bomb going off." All 12,000 residents of Summerland were ordered to evacuate immediately; at least 55 people were rescued by helicopter and roughly 10,000 sheltered in Penticton.

events.title: BC Declares Province-Wide State of Emergency; Civilian Dies Fleeing Bald Range Fire
events.detail: British Columbia declared a province-wide state of emergency as over 100 wildfires burned and more than 21,000 people evacuated. An 80-year-old woman died attempting to flee the Bald Range fire — the season's fifth confirmed death.

events.title: Second Wave of Mexican, Australian and New Zealand Firefighters Arrive
events.detail: More than 200 international firefighters from Mexico, with additional crews from Australia and New Zealand, arrived in British Columbia to reinforce exhausted domestic crews, bringing total international deployment since June to over 500 personnel from Mexico, Costa Rica, New Zealand and Australia.

events.title: Season Total Passes 4 Million Hectares Across 4,654 Fires
events.detail: Official CIFFC/Public Safety Canada figures put the season at 4,654 fires and 4,082,237 hectares burned nationally as of August 12 — led by the Northwest Territories (1,397,521 ha), Quebec (753,935 ha) and Ontario (732,080 ha). Activity remains below the five-year average by hectares, though the fire count exceeds the same point in 2025.

events.title: Alberta and BC Send Reinforcements to Quebec's Nord-du-Québec Fires
events.detail: With nearly 200 fires still burning in Quebec's Nord-du-Québec and Côte-Nord regions, approximately 100 firefighters from Alberta and British Columbia arrived to reinforce SOPFEU crews; Alberta also sent a 17-specialist Major Incident Management Team plus six water bombers and a bird-dog aircraft.

events.title: Summerland Evacuation Orders Lifted; 150 Structures Confirmed Lost
events.detail: Most evacuation orders around the Bald Range fire came down as residents began returning to Summerland, though the BC Wildfire Service still classified the roughly 220 km² blaze as burning out of control. Regional officials confirmed 150 structures damaged or destroyed — about 110 in the Faulder and Meadow Valley areas and 40 in the District of Summerland.

events.title: Ottawa's Season Funding Tally: $630M Across Aerial Fleet, Equipment, FireSmart
events.detail: Cumulative federal commitments for the season reached roughly $316.7 million over five years for a national aerial firefighting fleet through CIFFC, $256 million over five years for firefighting equipment, and $57.2 million over five years for Indigenous FireSmart programs — funding First Nations leaders say still arrived too slowly to prevent community losses.

events.title: Thunder Bay 36, 56 and Dryden 34/35 Evacuation Orders Revoked
events.detail: Effective 9:00am EDT, the evacuation order around active wildland fires Thunder Bay 36 & 56 and Dryden 34 & 35 was revoked, allowing displaced residents in the affected zones to begin returning after weeks of displacement.

events.title: Bradley Creek Wildfire Erupts Near Vernon, BC
events.detail: A human-caused wildfire ignited off Westside Road near Vernon, BC on July 31 and grew rapidly to over 2,600 hectares within days, jumping Highway 97. The Okanagan Indian Band and Splatsin First Nation issued evacuation orders covering IR 1 lands and surrounding properties at the north end of Okanagan Lake; BC Wildfire Service classified the fire as "being held" by August 9.

sources.name: City of Vernon — Bradley Creek Wildfire Updates

media.caption: Bradley Creek wildfire burns near Westside Road, Vernon, BC

events.title: Peachland Evacuation Orders Downgraded to Alert as Bald Range Fire Eases
events.detail: Central Okanagan Emergency Operations downgraded evacuation orders to alerts for Peachland and Electoral Area West effective 6pm August 14, allowing residents to return roughly one week after the Bald Range fire forced them out. The fire, by then nearly 20,000 hectares, remained active and out of control; no structural losses were reported in Peachland itself.

media.caption: Peachland, BC residents return home as Bald Range fire evacuation orders ease

events.title: Federal Ministers: 4,793 Fires, 4.1M Hectares Burned; 11,000 Still Under Evacuation Order
events.detail: Ministers Eleanor Olszewski and Mandy Gull-Masty delivered the government's August season update: 582 active wildfires nationally (31 out of control), 4,793 fires and over 4.1 million hectares burned season-to-date. Roughly 23,000 people have been evacuated overall, with about 11,000 still under evacuation order; 8,600 Indigenous people have been affected and 4,294 evacuated from 25 First Nations communities. Olszewski said activity has "grown and accelerated significantly" since the July 9 update, which had reported only 410,000 hectares burned.

media.caption: Minister Eleanor Olszewski provides the federal government's August 2026 wildfire season update

events.title: Bald Range Fire Grows to 24,820 Hectares Amid Erratic Winds, Still Out of Control
events.detail: BC Wildfire Service's August 22 update put the Bald Range fire west of Summerland at 24,820 hectares — up from roughly 22,000 hectares a week earlier — after 49 straight days without rain in the area. Eight evacuation orders and 13 evacuation alerts remain in place, with 32 properties still under order even as many Summerland and Peachland residents have returned home. The incident management team of 382 personnel, 15 helicopters and 77 pieces of heavy equipment maintained 24-hour operations ahead of a forecast Saturday thunderstorm with gusts to 70 km/h, prioritizing structure protection and Highway 97.

sources.name: BC Wildfire Service — Bald Range Incident (K51490)
Mission City Record / Black Press Media

media.caption: Bald Range wildfire burning west of Summerland, BC

events.title: B.C. Set for First August Rain, But Dry Lightning Risk Clouds Relief
events.detail: The Weather Network forecast B.C.'s first significant August rainfall for the weekend of Aug 22–23 — 10–15 mm for Vancouver, ~5 mm for Victoria and Kelowna, 5–10 mm for Kamloops — as a high-pressure system shifts east, dropping Interior temperatures more than 10°C and the Lower Mainland 5–7°C. Forecasters cautioned the rain would provide relief but remains insufficient to substantially improve fire conditions, and flagged dry lightning east of the Coastal Mountains as a fresh wildfire-risk concern; Kelowna has already logged 41 days above 30°C this year versus a typical 28.

media.caption: First August rainfall forecast to reach British Columbia this weekend

events.title: BC Extends Provincial State of Emergency Through Aug 29 as Bald Range Fire Stabilizes
events.detail: The Government of British Columbia extended its province-wide state of emergency — first declared Aug 8 amid the Bald Range fire crisis — for a further seven days through Saturday, Aug 29, citing continued elevated wildfire risk in the Okanagan and elsewhere even as most Bald Range evacuees have returned home. Officials said they have not yet needed to issue emergency orders under the extension but are keeping the powers available as conditions evolve. The Bald Range fire itself held essentially flat at 25,021 hectares through Aug 23 after 6–7mm of weekend rain moderated fire behaviour despite gusty winds, while BC Wildfire Service reported more than 150 active wildfires provincewide, nearly 60 of them out of control.

sources.name: Government of British Columbia — EMCR News Release

media.caption: West flank of the Bald Range wildfire from within the fire perimeter

events.title: Pear Lake Fire Surges Past 160,000 Hectares; Evacuation Orders Expand Along Highway 99
events.detail: The Pear Lake fire near Clinton, BC grew from 124,656 hectares on Aug 4 to 162,326 hectares by Aug 21 and 164,745 hectares by Aug 24, making it the season's second-largest blaze behind Thunder Bay 36. The Squamish-Lillooet Regional District expanded its evacuation order to cover more than 100 properties in the Pavilion Lake/Marble Canyon area, the Thompson-Nicola Regional District ordered out two properties on Highway 99, and the Bonaparte and Ts'kw'aylaxw First Nations evacuated several reserves — bringing total properties under order to nearly 200. Six evacuation orders and six evacuation alerts remain in place across the Big Bar fire complex; BC Wildfire Service crews conducted planned ignitions to remove fuel between the fire and control lines ahead of a forecast warming-and-drying trend starting Aug 24.

sources.name: Williams Lake Tribune / Black Press Media

media.caption: The Pear Lake wildfire burning in the Cariboo region of British Columbia

events.title: Ainslie Creek Fire Evacuation Response Downgraded as Growth Slows to 67,722 Hectares
events.detail: The Thompson-Nicola Regional District downgraded its evacuation response for the out-of-control Ainslie Creek fire west of the Coquihalla near Merritt after two days of cool temperatures and high humidity slowed fire growth to just 15 hectares between Aug 23 and 24. The evacuation order covering 61 properties around Spius, Petit and Prospect creeks was downgraded to alert, and 620 addressed properties in Electoral Areas M and N were given the all-clear, though roughly 58 properties along Coldwater Road/Patchett Road remain on evacuation order. The fire — out of control since late July and one of BC's three remaining 'wildfires of note' — stood at 67,722 hectares as of Aug 24 with no reported structure losses. This fire had not previously appeared in this tracker despite burning since late July.

media.caption: Planned ignition operations east of Highway 1 in the Fraser Canyon at the Ainslie Creek wildfire

events.title: Bald Range Fire Grows to 25,171 Hectares as Peachland Evacuation Alerts Fully Rescinded
events.detail: The Bald Range fire near Summerland, BC grew slightly to 25,171 hectares as of a 4pm update on Aug 25, with the BC Wildfire Service warning that progressively warmer, drier conditions over the following 24 hours would make smoke and flame more visible on the active west flank near Isintok Lake. All remaining evacuation alerts for properties in and around Peachland were rescinded after officials determined the threat had passed, leaving 6 evacuation orders and 10 evacuation alerts in place — down from 8 orders and 13 alerts a week earlier. An evacuation order remains for Faulder, where dozens of homes were destroyed earlier in the fire's run. 322 firefighters are assigned to the blaze with 24-hour coverage.

media.caption: Bald Range wildfire activity near Summerland, BC

events.title: 476 Firefighters Battle Pear Lake Blaze as Warming Trend Threatens Renewed Growth
events.detail: The Pear Lake fire in the Cariboo held at 164,745 hectares as of Aug 24, with the BC Wildfire Service reporting 476 firefighting personnel, 89 structure protection workers, 120 heavy equipment units and 21 helicopters assigned. Crews continued building machine guard and conducting planned ignitions south of Pavilion Mountain to bolster containment lines. A warming and drying trend expected to begin Monday could increase fire activity despite weekend rainfall. Six evacuation orders and six evacuation alerts remain at the Big Bar complex; the Village of Clinton rescinded most of its evacuation alert but kept some properties on alert due to flood risk.

media.caption: Pear Lake wildfire in the Cariboo region of BC

events.title: B.C. Down to Three 'Wildfires of Note' as Lightning-Sparked Surge Recedes
events.detail: British Columbia's list of 'wildfires of note' shrank to three — Ainslie Creek, Pear Lake and Bald Range — after the Brunswick Creek blaze west of the Fraser Canyon was removed following a reduced spread threat and downgraded evacuation orders. Provincewide active wildfires fell to roughly 160, down from a peak above 180 after a weekend storm produced about 11,000 lightning strikes across the province. Rain over the same weekend helped crews gain ground on several fronts even as officials warned of a warming, drying trend into the following week.

media.caption: Wildfire activity in British Columbia

events.title: Thunder Bay 36 Fire Remeasured at 301,240 Hectares as Mexican Crews Assist Rinker Lake Complex
events.detail: Updated perimeter mapping put the Thunder Bay 36 fire, the largest in Ontario's recorded history, at 301,240 hectares as of Aug 24 — down from earlier estimates near 320,000 hectares — though it remains not under control. Firefighters from Ontario and Mexico continued hotspot suppression across the Rinker Lake Complex using helicopter bucket and belly-tank operations amid low fire activity. Elsewhere in the Atikokan cluster, Fort Frances 14 (51,768 ha) shifted to 'being held' while Fort Frances 15 (42,273 ha) and Dryden 35 (30,158 ha, revised upward) continued to be observed or burn out of control. The Northwest Region reported 64 active wildland fires — 5 not under control, 3 being held, 12 under control and 44 being observed — with two new small fires spotted near Rossport over the weekend.

events.title: Bradley Creek Fire: North Okanagan Cancels State of Local Emergency
events.detail: The Regional District of North Okanagan cancelled its State of Local Emergency and rescinded the evacuation alert for properties in Electoral Area B tied to the Bradley Creek fire, effective Aug 24, acting on a recommendation from the BC Wildfire Service. The ~2,650-hectare fire near Vernon has been held since Aug 9. RDNO reminded residents that wildfire risk remains province-wide and encouraged continued use of the Alertable app for emergency notifications.

sources.name: Vernon Morning Star / Black Press Media

media.caption: Evacuation alert rescinded notice for the Bradley Creek fire area

events.title: Neskantaga First Nation Evacuated a Second Time After Sewage Floods Its Only Nursing Station
events.detail: Neskantaga First Nation's chief and council declared a local state of emergency on Aug 4 and evacuated the fly-in community of 350 in Northwestern Ontario after raw sewage backed up into the basement of its only nursing station, forcing the health centre to close. Chief Gary Quisess said a federal contractor performing repairs caused the backup after declining the community's offer to use its own sewage pumping truck first — the second evacuation of the community in a single summer, coming just days after residents had returned home from the wildfire evacuation that displaced them in July. It was also the second condemnation of the health centre in two years, after 2025 diesel contamination forced a similar closure. A temporary duplex-trailer nursing station has since been set up.

media.caption: Temporary duplex-trailer nursing station used after Neskantaga's health centre was flooded

events.title: Lightning-Caused Ezra Creek Fire Erupts North of Castlegar, BC
events.detail: A new lightning-caused wildfire, Ezra Creek, was discovered August 25 on Mount Sentinel above the Tarrys and Thrums area, north of Castlegar in BC's Southeast Fire Centre. It grew rapidly to an initial estimate of 200 hectares within a day, prompting BC Wildfire Service to deploy initial-attack rappel crews, 9 airtankers (4 Q400s and 3 CL-215T skimmers) and 2 birddog coordination aircraft; more accurate mapping later revised the size down to 116 hectares. Retardant lines held the fire's eastern flank overnight into August 27 with no outside growth observed, though it remains classified as out of control. No structures or infrastructure are currently threatened and no evacuation orders or alerts have been issued.

sources.name: Grand Forks Gazette / Black Press Media

media.caption: Ezra Creek wildfire burning north of Castlegar, BC
media.source: BC Wildfire Service / Grand Forks Gazette

events.title: Rinker Lake Complex Command Transfers to Thunder Bay Fire Management HQ as Activity Eases
events.detail: With wildland fire activity across the Rinker Lake Complex remaining low, the Perin Incident Management Team transferred command of Thunder Bay 36, Dryden 34 and Dryden 35 to the Thunder Bay Fire Management Headquarters on August 25 — a step that reflects reduced fire behaviour even though all three fires remain classified as not under control. As of the transition, Thunder Bay 36 stood at roughly 301,000-307,000 hectares (estimates vary by remapping pass), Dryden 34 at approximately 45,800 hectares and Dryden 35 at approximately 30,158 hectares. The Northwest Fire Region counted 64 active fires overall on August 25 (3 not under control, 4 being held, 12 under control, 45 being observed), and a separate incident management team similarly stood down over the Atikokan-area Fort Frances 13/14/15 cluster on August 26. NOTAMs remain in effect around Fort Frances 14 and Thunder Bay 36.

media.caption: Waterbomber aircraft used in Northwestern Ontario wildfire suppression operations

events.title: Crews Conduct Controlled Burn on ZF028 Fire North of Behchokǫ̀, NWT
events.detail: NWT Fire crews conducted a planned ignition north of Russell Channel, roughly 13 km north of Behchokǫ̀, to burn out fuel ahead of wildfire ZF028 and create a buffer for the community. The operation reached 50% completion on August 21 before changing weather forced a pause, then resumed and reached 50% again by August 24 after at least 7mm of weekend rain aided the fight; crews planned to continue when conditions allow. NWT Fire described the burn as a pro-active tactic and said there is no threat to communities or infrastructure at this time, though smoke remains visible from Behchokǫ̀.

media.caption: Controlled burn operation on the ZF028 fire near Behchokǧà, NWT

events.title: British Columbia Ends Wildfire State of Emergency Two Days Early
events.detail: British Columbia ended its province-wide wildfire state of emergency at 3:25 PM on August 27 — two days ahead of the scheduled August 29 extension deadline — after emergency management officials advised the declaration's powers were no longer needed. The state of emergency, first declared August 8 as the Bald Range fire and other blazes forced fast-moving evacuations, was never actually invoked to exercise emergency powers, according to Emergency Management and Climate Readiness Minister Kelly Greene. Ending the declaration has no effect on the roughly 206 wildfires still burning provincewide or on the evacuation orders, evacuation alerts and local states of emergency that individual regional districts and First Nations continue to maintain.

media.caption: British Columbia ends its wildfire state of emergency

events.title: Bald Range Fire Held at 25,185 Hectares as More Evacuation Orders Rescinded
events.detail: The Bald Range fire west of Summerland remained held at 25,185 hectares as of Aug 28, per the BC Wildfire Service, with 379 firefighters, 7 helicopters, 43 pieces of heavy equipment and a 5-person structure protection crew assigned. Rain and cooler temperatures moved into the Okanagan Valley over the weekend — the fire's first meaningful precipitation since it broke out Aug 7. The Regional District of Okanagan-Similkameen rescinded the evacuation order for the area south of Princeton-Summerland Road near Agur Lake and narrowed the Bathville Road order to just two properties (21430 and 21442 Bathville Rd), while the Penticton Indian Band rescinded all remaining evacuation orders and alerts on its affected reserve lands.

sources.name: Salmon Arm Observer / Black Press Media
Vernon Morning Star / Black Press Media

media.caption: Bald Range wildfire west of Summerland, BC
media.source: Salmon Arm Observer / BC Wildfire Service

events.title: Eabametoong, Gull Bay and Lac Des Mille Lacs Evacuees All Return Home as Ontario Fire Count Eases to 59
events.detail: As of Aug 28, all wildfire evacuees from Eabametoong First Nation, Gull Bay First Nation and Lac Des Mille Lacs First Nation had returned home, according to Prepared Ontario — closing out evacuations that began in mid-July and had sent nearly 950 Eabametoong members and hundreds of Gull Bay residents to host communities including Niagara Falls, Fort Frances, Kenora and Thunder Bay. No injuries or property damage were reported among the returning evacuees. Separately, Northwestern Ontario's active fire count eased to 59 (6 not under control, 3 being held, 12 under control, 38 being observed) after three small new starts — Fort Frances 68, Dryden 64 and Sioux Lookout 115 — were confirmed the same day; the Rinker Lake Complex (Thunder Bay 36, Dryden 34, Dryden 35) remains not under control despite low fire activity.

media.caption: Waterbomber aircraft supporting Northwestern Ontario wildfire operations

events.title: Pear Lake Fire Grows to 166,111 Hectares as Crews Work Big Bar Mountain Flank
events.detail: BC Wildfire Service pegged the Pear Lake fire at 166,111 hectares as of Aug 30, up 182 hectares from the prior day's 165,929-hectare estimate — the season's second-largest wildfire continues slow, steady growth. No overnight rain fell and only minimal precipitation was recorded through the day, leaving crown fire activity possible wherever rain did not reach the fireline; the blaze remained most active around Big Bar Mountain. Crews spent Aug 29 completing a set of small planned ignitions to bring the fire's edge to workable ground north of Separating Lake, and continued mop-up, patrols and direct attacks along the south containment line near Kelly Lake, Robertson Creek and Allen Creek. No new evacuation orders were reported.

media.caption: A BC Wildfire Service crew member works a containment line on the south flank of the Pear Lake fire off Highway 97

events.title: Two New Fires Ignite Near Sioux Narrows and Blue Lake Provincial Park as NW Ontario Holds at 59 Active
events.detail: Ontario's Aviation, Forest Fire and Emergency Services confirmed two new wildfire starts in its Sunday-night report: Kenora 34, a 0.1-hectare fire on an island on Cameron Lake southeast of Sioux Narrows, listed not under control; and Dryden 66, a 0.1-hectare fire near Brownie Lake about 7 km west of the Blue Lake Provincial Park campground, listed as being held. The two new starts left the Northwest Fire Region's active count unchanged at 59 (4 not under control, 4 being held, 12 under control, 39 being observed), as other small fires were closed out elsewhere in the region over the same period. The Rinker Lake Complex — Thunder Bay 36 (301,240 ha), Dryden 34 (45,800 ha) and Dryden 35 (30,158 ha), a combined 377,198 ha — remains not under control though activity stays low; command remains with Thunder Bay Fire Management Headquarters, with crews using helicopter bucketing to suppress remaining hotspots.

media.caption: Northwest Fire Region wildfire operations update

events.title: Northwestern Ontario Active Fire Count Eases to 56 as Rinker Complex Holds Steady
events.detail: Northwestern Ontario's active wildfire count eased to 56 as of Sept. 1 (3 not under control, 3 being held, 12 under control, 38 being observed), down from 59 in late August, with no new fires confirmed. The Rinker Lake Complex — Thunder Bay 36 (301,240 ha), Dryden 34 (45,800 ha) and Dryden 35 (30,158 ha), a combined 377,198 ha — remains not under control, though fire behaviour across the complex has stayed on the low end in recent days as crews continue helicopter bucketing on hotspots and demobilize equipment no longer needed.

media.caption: Waterbomber aircraft supporting Northwestern Ontario wildfire operations

events.title: National Season Total Reaches 5,248 Fires and 4.49 Million Hectares
events.detail: CIFFC's season-to-date figures as of August 31 put Canada at 5,248 fires and 4,492,283 hectares burned nationally — up from 4,793 fires and 4.1 million hectares on August 18. The Northwest Territories remained the single largest contributor at 1,694,002 hectares across 288 fires, followed by Quebec (753,935 ha), Ontario (743,066 ha) and British Columbia (476,586 ha, reflecting the Bald Range, Pear Lake and Ainslie Creek fires).

events.title: Two New Fires Confirmed Near Miller Lake and Detour Lake; NW Ontario Rises to 58 Active
events.detail: Ontario's Aviation, Forest Fire and Emergency Services confirmed two new starts in its September 2 evening report: Kenora 35, a 0.1-hectare fire north of Glorious Lake about 2.5 km southwest of Miller Lake, not under control; and Red Lake 28, a 0.1-hectare fire at the northeast end of Detour Lake southwest of Lee Lake, also not under control. The additions pushed the Northwest Fire Region's active count to 58 (5 not under control, 3 being held, 12 under control, 38 being observed). The Rinker Lake Complex — Thunder Bay 36 (301,240 ha), Dryden 34 (45,800 ha) and Dryden 35 (30,158 ha) — remained not under control with fire behaviour on the lower end despite visible smoke.

media.caption: Northwest Fire Region wildfire operations update

events.title: Pear Lake, Ainslie Creek and Brunswick Creek Fires Lose 'Wildfire of Note' Status
events.detail: BC Wildfire Service removed the Pear Lake fire (166,131.9 ha, near Clinton) and the Boston Bar-area complex — Ainslie Creek (67,722.48 ha) and Brunswick Creek (9,266.86 ha) — from its 'wildfires of note' list as of Sept 3, with Ainslie Creek and Brunswick Creek both classified as being held. Much of Pear Lake's perimeter is now secure, though heat remains within it and the fire is still officially out of control amid extreme drought conditions in soil and timber across the area. Evacuation orders and alerts remain in effect across several regional districts and First Nations for both fire areas. BC Wildfire Service reported 355 firefighters, 5 structure-protection personnel, 48 heavy equipment units and 10 helicopters assigned to Pear Lake. A Sept 3 CBC News report additionally characterized Ainslie Creek's downgrade to 'held' status as removing BC's last fire still classified as a major wildfire of concern, though evacuation orders for two First Nations remained tied to the neighboring Pear Lake fire.

events.title: Seven New Fires Confirmed as NW Ontario Active Count Rises to 62
events.detail: Ontario's Aviation, Forest Fire and Emergency Services confirmed seven new starts on Sept 3: Dryden 68 (0.1 ha, near Daniels Lake) was extinguished the same day; Nipigon 108 (0.5 ha, near Eskwanonwatin Lake), Fort Frances 69/70/71/72 (0.1 ha each, clustered near Bearpaw Lake and Highway 502) and Thunder Bay 86 (0.1 ha, Max Lake island) remained not under control. The additions pushed the Northwest Fire Region's active count to 62 (9 not under control, 3 being held, 12 under control, 38 being observed). The Rinker Lake Complex — Thunder Bay 36 (301,240 ha), Dryden 34 (45,800 ha) and Dryden 35 (30,158 ha), a combined 377,240 ha — remained not under control with a NOTAM still in effect around Thunder Bay 36.

events.title: Bald Range Fire Area Restriction Order Rescinded as Activity Decreases
events.detail: BC Wildfire Service rescinded its area restriction order for the Bald Range fire west of Summerland, effective Sept 4, after fire behaviour and activity decreased to the point firefighting personnel no longer need to restrict public access to operate safely. The fire remains mapped at over 25,000 hectares. The Service reminded the public that fire-damaged trees may be unstable and hot ash pits can persist long after flames die down, and asked that any smoke from green fuel or outside the fire's perimeter be reported.

events.title: Bald Range Fire Downgraded to 'Under Control' as Summerland Recovery Measures Begin
events.detail: BC Wildfire Service classified the Bald Range fire west of Summerland as 'under control' as of Aug 31, its most advanced status tier since erupting Aug 7 and forcing the evacuation of over 20,000 people across the Regional District of Okanagan-Similkameen. The fire remains mapped at more than 25,000 hectares. Separately, the regional district approved recovery measures for residents who lost homes — including 5-year allowances to live in RVs on their properties and halved permit fees for rebuilding — after the fire destroyed roughly 150 structures.

events.title: TNRD and SLRD Downgrade Remaining Pear Lake-Area Evacuation Orders to Alerts
events.detail: Effective 4 p.m. Sept 3, the Thompson-Nicola Regional District downgraded its last two evacuation orders — one property on West Pavilion Road tied to the French Bar Creek fire, and the no-addressed-property Pavilion Mountain area (south of Kelly Lake and Clinton) tied to the Pear Lake fire — to evacuation alerts. The Squamish-Lillooet Regional District downgraded its own Pear Lake-area order the same day. 142 addressed properties in TNRD Electoral Areas E and I remain under evacuation alert, and evacuation orders issued separately by the Whispering Pines/Clinton Indian Band and Stswecem'c Xget'tem First Nation for their own lands remained in effect. Pear Lake is mapped at roughly 166,132 hectares.

events.title: Matthew Creek Fire Area Restriction Reduced Near Kimberley
events.detail: BC Wildfire Service reduced the size of its area restriction zone around the Matthew Creek fire (N11020), roughly 10 km west of Kimberley in the East Kootenay, effective 1 p.m. MT Sept 3, after weeks of firefighting combined with favourable weather reduced fire activity. The fire, discovered Aug 15 and suspected lightning-caused, is mapped at 1,826 hectares and has been classified as being held since Aug 19. The revised, smaller restriction remains enforceable through Oct 31 and covers only Crown land; the Matthew Creek Forest Service Road stays closed to public travel.

events.title: New Small Fires Confirmed Near Nipigon and Long Lake 58 First Nation
events.detail: Ontario's Aviation, Forest Fire and Emergency Services confirmed Nipigon 108, a 0.5-hectare fire not under control roughly 21 km west of Highway 585 near Eskwanonwatin Lake, on Sept 4. By the evening of Sept 5, three further new starts had been confirmed in the Northwest Region, including Nipigon 111, a 0.2-hectare fire being held about half a kilometre northwest of Wolf Street in Long Lake 58 First Nation. The additions kept Northwestern Ontario's active fire count near 62, with the Rinker Lake Complex (Thunder Bay 36, Dryden 34, Dryden 35 — 377,240 ha combined) still not under control amid otherwise low regional fire activity.
